name: Quran learning
title: Free Quran Quizzes, Search & Study Tools | Moongazer
heading: Eight ways to spend time with the Quran
description: Test your surah recognition, search Arabic or English wording, trace themes across passages, and read parables and revelation context with sources right beside the text.
intro: Whether you have five minutes for a daily surah puzzle or an hour to sit with a parable, these eight tools meet you where you are. Pick a quiz when you want a quick check, wording search when a phrase is on the tip of your tongue, or a guided reading when you want to slow down with commentary.
guidance: Start with the verses themselves before opening any note or diagram. Quranic text, translations, and classical commentary are always kept clearly separate from our questions and visual aids, so you can see where the scripture ends and the study tool begins.

items.reason: Use opening-ayah clues to recognize a surah, then inspect the reference behind the answer.
Move from chapter recognition into comparing the shared theme of three selected passages.

paths.title: Find wording, then explore a theme

items.reason: Search Arabic text or Pickthall's English translation when you have wording or an ayah reference.

items.label: Ayah Threads theme library
items.reason: Read a theme's three ayat when your starting point is a subject; solve its puzzle first to keep the surprise.

paths.title: Read a selected account in context

items.reason: Open a prophet's profile for selected Quran passages and a short reading check.
Compare named reports while keeping transmitted occasions, general context and later responses distinct.

questions.question: Which tool should I use for an exact Quran phrase?
questions.answer: Open Is It in the Quran? to search Arabic text, Pickthall's English translation, or a specific verse reference. Keep in mind that a blank result only means those exact words did not match—the same idea may appear under different wording.

questions.question: Where can I explore diagrams or places?
questions.answer: Parables of the Quran pairs each passage with a simple visual map of its imagery, while Places in the Quran links verses to geography and leaves uncertain sites unpinned on the map.

name: Seerah & history
title: Seerah & Islamic History Explorers | Moongazer
heading: Read Seerah and Islamic history with the sources open
description: Trace the Prophet's life ﷺ year by year, weigh primary reports in short cases, and follow Islamic civilization across nine regions from 661 to 1648 CE.
intro: Good history starts by looking closely at what the sources actually say. Follow the major turns of the Prophet's life ﷺ on a timeline, step into a short Seerah case to test what a report establishes, or zoom out across ten centuries of cities, trade, and scholarship.
guidance: Not every historical date carries the same certainty. Where a year is conventional or approximate, the notes say so plainly—and when two events sit near each other on a timeline, we keep their context separate unless the sources link them directly.

paths.title: Follow an event into its reports

items.reason: Browse a sourced chronology, then open an event to read the reports and date notes.
Practice deciding which conclusion a selected evidence set actually supports.
Read selected records across regions and inspect two date bands together.
Explore a related geographical reading while distinguishing a modern map context from an exact ancient location.

paths.title: Turn reading into an ordering exercise

items.reason: Use the timeline as a reading reference before trying a short chronology task.

items.label: Which came first? (Seerah Timeline)
items.reason: Arrange four events from the prophetic mission, then compare their sources and approximate dates.

questions.question: Are these complete history courses?
questions.answer: No. They are selected reading tools. The Seerah timeline and the common-claims checks focus on particular events and questions, while the civilization timeline presents twenty-four selected records across nine regions.

questions.question: What should I check before treating a date as exact?
questions.answer: Read the individual event's dating and source notes. A report may support an event without giving its displayed calendar year. The tools retain that distinction rather than making every record appear equally precise.

name: Prayer & everyday practice
title: Salah Meanings, Hifz Planning & Everyday Akhlaq | Moongazer
heading: Bring what you read into prayer and daily life
description: Learn the words you recite in salah, plan a realistic hifz and revision routine, calculate zakat step by step, and think through everyday character dilemmas.
intro: Knowledge settles when it meets daily habit. Walk through the meanings of your prayer from opening takbir to salam, map out a hifz schedule that protects your revision first, work through a real-world akhlaq dilemma, or calculate your zakat with every scholarly option clearly labelled.
guidance: Use these tools as practical companions, not verdicts. The hifz planner estimates time based on your own pace, the akhlaq scenarios are conversation starters rather than rulings, and the zakat calculator shows its working so you can verify complex questions with a scholar.

paths.title: Make space for a reading session

items.reason: Choose one of fifteen recitation-meaning lessons and compare its Arabic, meaning and source notes.
Estimate how new Quran study and revision fit around the session time you provide.
Read a character scenario, consider a choice and inspect its imagined consequence.

items.label: Everyday Akhlaq business scenarios
items.reason: Apply the same careful reading to fictional business cases without treating them as transaction certification.

paths.title: Check the evidence before a conclusion

items.label: Common claims (Is It in the Quran?)
items.reason: Check a claim people often make against the exact text before you share it.
Compare a report and its stated limits when studying the context around a passage.

questions.question: Does Understand Your Salah teach every legal detail of prayer?
questions.answer: It focuses on selected recitation meanings and narrated wordings. It includes local Al-Fatiha audio, while the other lessons are text-based. Use its source notes and qualified instruction for practice questions or legal differences.

questions.question: Can I use the business cases as a ruling on my transaction?
questions.answer: No. The business scenarios in Everyday Akhlaq present fictional educational cases. Real arrangements can involve facts and obligations outside an exercise, so the app does not certify transactions or provide personalized legal or financial advice.

name: Games & family activities
title: Islamic Word Games, Escape Rooms & Family Halaqa | Moongazer
heading: Play together, then open the passage
description: Solve Quran escape rooms, sort sixteen Quranic words into four hidden groups, race a Seerah chronology, or sit down for a ten-minute family halaqa.
intro: Learning sticks better when people are talking and thinking together. Gather around one screen for a Quran escape room, test your eye for patterns in Word Groups, or pick a ten-minute Family Halaqa pack with a verse, a question, and a shared activity.
guidance: Every game here runs straight in the browser with no sign-ups, leaderboards, or profiles. Read the clues aloud, adapt the wording for younger kids, and treat the score as a light prompt to open the verses afterward.

paths.title: Discuss a puzzle on one screen

items.reason: Work through reading and recognition puzzles together, using the source shelf and hints when useful.
Compare possible connections between terms, then inspect the board's intended groups and readings.
Pick a suggested age band, topic and time, then work through the pack's three-part session.
Continue a conversation with a fictional character scenario rather than asking for personal experiences.

items.label: Which came first? (Seerah Timeline)
items.reason: Arrange four events using buttons and compare the answer with the cited reports.
Return to a broader chronology when you want to read an event in more detail.

questions.question: Are these synchronized multiplayer games?
questions.answer: No. They run in the browser on the device being used. People can discuss an escape room or family activity together on one screen; the collection does not create a live multiplayer session or player accounts.

questions.question: How should I choose an activity for children?
questions.answer: Family Halaqa includes suggested age bands and times. An adult can read aloud, adapt vocabulary and let participants pass. Keep discussion examples fictional and choose a pack that suits the group rather than treating the age label as a strict requirement.
